subject: health
title: Guided practice: reliable health information
essentialQuestion: How can understanding whole-person wellbeing and trusted support help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool
keyPoints: Reliable health information names who created it, uses evidence, has a recent review date, and separates education from advertising or a promise to sell something.
Check authorship, expertise, evidence, currency, uncertainty, and incentive before using a health message; confidence, popularity, and testimonials are not substitutes for support.
For reliable health information, a strong response distinguishes fact from assumption, uses a fictional or public case, and includes a safe next step or appropriate source of support.
privacySafeScenario: Create a private-safe support map and a reliable-information checklist.
studentTask: Compare two supplied fictional messages about reliable health information. Build a four-row check for source or author, evidence, date or context, and incentive; then choose the stronger message, cite two details, and state what remains uncertain.
knowledgeCheck: In two or three sentences, explain the most important distinction in reliable health information; use one lesson fact and name the evidence, safety check, or support route that makes the explanation dependable.
completionCriteria: The response completes every named part of the reliable health information task using the supplied fictional or public case.
The response uses at least two accurate details from the lesson instruction and distinguishes evidence from assumption.
The response gives a safe, feasible next step or support route and does not depend on private disclosure, body comparison, or recorded media proof.
adaptationChoices: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required. Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model. Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits. Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options. Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media. Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
extensionChallenge: Apply reliable health information under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work.

trustedAdultNote: Direct urgent safety or health concerns to a trusted adult or qualified professional.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice one safe, optional example of reliable health information in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, or private disclosure is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
